name: Collagenmaxxing

lead: Collagenmaxxing is the looksmaxxing term for stacking nutrients that supply or support collagen, the structural protein of skin, to look younger and have smoother, clearer skin. A typical stack is hydrolyzed collagen peptides, vitamin C, the amino acid glycine and enough dietary protein, sometimes alongside topical retinoids or microneedling.

Believers say the stack firms and hydrates skin and helps acne scars and post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation fade. Controlled research on oral collagen exists but is mixed, and reviewers describe the evidence base as limited by study quality; the numerical gains quoted on forums are users' own estimates.

paras: Practitioners usually take collagen peptide powder daily, often with a vitamin C source, add glycine in the evening, and keep protein intake up. Some add taurine and zinc. Many pair it with topical routines such as tretinoin or microneedling for the 'collagen induction' effect. Posters report watching for changes over a few weeks to a couple of months.

Collagen peptides are a food-type supplement and are generally well tolerated; they come from bovine, porcine or marine sources, which matters for allergies and dietary rules. Products are lightly regulated as supplements, so contents vary. Retinoids and microneedling, when added to the stack, carry their own irritation and sun-sensitivity risks.

lead: Collagenmaxxing is a looksmaxxing term for a nutrition-and-skincare approach aimed at collagen, the structural protein that gives skin much of its firmness. People use it to improve skin texture, hydration and youthful appearance, and to help acne scars and dark marks fade. [1][2]

A commonly shared stack on looksmax.org combines collagen peptides, vitamin C and zinc, glycine and taurine, with the claim that these supply the amino-acid building blocks and cofactors fibroblasts need to make collagen. [1] Other threads pair the approach with tretinoin and microneedling, which users describe as stimulating collagen production from the outside. [3]

Research on oral collagen is mixed. Two meta-analyses of randomized trials, one in 2021 and one in 2023, reported that hydrolyzed collagen taken by mouth improved skin hydration and elasticity compared with placebo, while their authors also noted bias in the included trials and called for larger studies. [4][4] Wikipedia's collagen article, citing a 2025 review, states that no clinical evidence supports oral collagen for wrinkles or skin aging and explains that ingested collagen is digested into peptides and amino acids. [5][5]

paras: The term follows the '-maxxing' convention of looksmaxxing culture: maximize one attribute, here collagen. A thread on fading scars and post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation (PIH) lists a 'direct collagen support' group (collagen peptides, glycine, taurine) alongside vitamin C and zinc as co-factors. [1]

The author's reasoning is that collagen peptides supply hydroxyproline, proline and glycine, glycine supports sleep and healing, and taurine protects fibroblasts. Another poster in the same thread asked where the quoted percentage 'boosts' come from, and the author replied that they were legitimate; no source was given. [1]

Other looksmax.org threads carry titles such as an 'ultimate collagenmaxxing guide' and a 'fastest way to collagenmax', showing that the term is used for a broad family of routines rather than a single protocol. [6][7]

Collagen is the most abundant structural protein in the body; types I and III make up over 90 percent of human collagen, and type I is the main form in skin, tendon and bone. Collagen chains are modified in the cell by enzymes that need vitamin C as a cofactor, and prolonged vitamin C deficiency impairs collagen synthesis and causes scurvy. [5] This biochemistry is the basis of the vitamin C component in collagenmaxxing stacks.

Skin ageing involves dermal thinning, loss of collagen, degeneration of elastic fibers and reduced hydration, and chronic UV exposure further disorganizes both collagen and elastic fibers. Wikipedia notes that collagen gives tensile strength while elastin allows stretch and recoil, and that age-related loss of elasticity is linked more closely to elastin decline than to collagen loss. [5]

Collagen peptides (hydrolyzed collagen) are made by breaking down gelatin further; sources include cattle, pigs, chickens and fish, usually from meat and leather industry by-products, with fish-derived versions chosen by some for religious or dietary reasons. They are used in foods, capsule shells and cosmetics. [8]

Glycine, taurine and zinc are added in forum guides for their roles in sleep, antioxidant protection of fibroblasts and wound healing respectively, per the guide's author. [1] Protein intake is included on the premise that skin needs amino acids to build collagen. Many users add topical tretinoin and microneedling, which are marketed or discussed as ways to induce new collagen. [3]

Forum users describe collagenmaxxing as part of a broader anti-aging routine. One post titled as a success story describes a 28-year-old being guessed at about 24 after combining anti-aging skincare and supplements; the poster was unsure which part of the routine mattered and had also had jaw surgery. [2]

Separate guides treat microneedling plus topical tretinoin as the main collagen-induction method, describe it as far cheaper than clinic lasers, peels or professional needling, and cite a study on acne scars as support. [3]

Wikipedia's collagen entry states that digested collagen does not reach skin intact, that no clinical evidence as of 2025 supports oral collagen for wrinkles, and that cosmetics often use hydrolyzed collagen or small peptides on the basis of an unproven belief that absorption improves. [5][5]

A 2021 systematic review and meta-analysis in the International Journal of Dermatology pooled 19 randomized, placebo-controlled trials with 1,125 participants aged 20 to 70, about 95 percent women. It reported improvements in skin hydration, elasticity and wrinkles with oral hydrolyzed collagen, and its authors concluded that 90 days of ingestion reduces skin ageing. [4] A published commentary raised concerns about heterogeneity among the included studies. [4]

A 2023 meta-analysis in Nutrients pooled 26 randomized trials with 1,721 participants and found significant improvements in hydration and elasticity versus placebo. The hydration effect varied by collagen source and duration, the review identified several biases in the trials, and the authors said larger trials are needed. [4]
The European Food Safety Authority found in 2011 no established cause-and-effect link between collagen hydrolysate and joint maintenance, according to Wikipedia. [8]

The study cited in the looksmax.org guide is a 2014 report in the Journal of Cutaneous and Aesthetic Surgery on 49 patients with atrophic acne scars. Participants received one subcision, then alternating dermaroller microneedling and 15 percent trichloroacetic acid peels every two weeks for six sessions each, with topical tretinoin 0.05 percent used during and after microneedling. [9]

Physicians graded scars before and after. Of 16 patients with grade 4 scars, 10 improved to grade 2 and 6 to grade 3; all 11 patients with grade 2 scars were scar-free at the end; improvements held at one year. Ice-pick scars changed little, and adverse effects were mild, including PIH in three patients. The study had no control group, so the contribution of individual components cannot be separated. [9]

Wikipedia describes microneedling, also called collagen induction therapy, as repeated puncture of the skin with sterile needles used for scarring and acne, with infection the main concern when done without proper hygiene; the CDC reported three HIV diagnoses in April 2024 among patients of one spa offering microneedling with platelet-rich plasma. [10]

Collagen peptides are food-type products from animal sources, so allergy and dietary restrictions are relevant; Wikipedia notes injected gelatin can cause severe allergic reactions in some people, which is a different route from oral intake. [8] Supplements are lightly regulated, so product contents vary. Retinoids and microneedling add irritation and sun-sensitivity considerations that are separate from the supplements.

No studies found for the 'collagenmaxxing' stack as a whole. Related research on single components includes the meta-analyses of oral hydrolyzed collagen described above [4][4] and the uncontrolled study of subcision, microneedling, peels and tretinoin in acne scars. [9]
